items.requirement: An isoSPI (isolated SPI) transceiver pair or a digital isolator between the ADBMS1818ASWAZ-RL and the measurement coprocessor's SPI1, rated 85 V DC working or more (V189). Answered under Raised by P1: V289: A digital isolator on direct SPI, rated 85 V DC working or more (V189). Its current is for research (owner, 2026-10-01). Its pack side runs from an always-on supply referenced to the pack negative, not from the ADBMS1818's regulator, which is off while the monitor sleeps; the same supply gives the ADBMS1818 an external VREG, and V+ of 16 V or more for packs under 16 V. That supply is a function of R9 (owner, 2026-10-02)
items.source: V189; IOBoard.md, Cell monitor isolation; Pins.md
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: An always-on supply referenced to the ESC pack's negative. It runs the isolator's pack side while the ADBMS1818ASWAZ-RL sleeps, so the monitor can be woken over SPI, gives the ADBMS1818 an external VREG, and gives V+ of 16 V or more for packs under 16 V, from 1 cell (V181) to 16 cells at 67.2 V (F15) (V289, owner, 2026-10-02)

found_values.value: No finite longest stall with the firmware as written; 900 ms for one main-loop pass in which the USB host stops reading. (a) One flash window a pass: out_store_tick() runs once a pass, and out_store_reclaim() only on a pass where the tick returned OUT_STORE_IDLE (main.c:1049, :1083); the longest window is one 4 kB sector erase, 400 ms maximum (packaged-part figure, W25Q16JV-DTR revision I tSE; the die's figure is not known). (b) Each console printf after it (main.c:1059-1067, :1084) blocks in pico-sdk 2.3.0 stdio_usb_out_chars(), which leaves its loop only when no space is free and more than PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed since the last accepted chunk (stdio_usb.c:122); last_avail_time is reset at each accepted chunk (stdio_usb.c:118); the default is 500,000 us (stdio_usb.h:31-33) and no file under firmware/ or shared/ overrides it. (c) 400 ms erase plus one 500 ms blocked write: 900 ms. (d) With a host that keeps accepting slowly, each accepted chunk restarts the 500 ms, so the stall has no bound but the message length. (e) At boot, up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 erases (main.c:937-942, out_store.h:122) before can_start(): 800 ms plus prints, counted only if the watchdog runs by then. Q8 moves the output binding to an I2C FRAM (owner, 2026-09-29), which removes the erase once the firmware follows it; the firmware in this checkout still erases flash

Section 8.1.2.3: 'Appropriate margin is built into the design to tolerate up to 1000ppm variation in the XOSC frequency'; section 8.1.2.6: the PLLs drive clocks at their maximum 'as long as the reference clock is accurate to 1000ppm'. Looser limits: USB full speed 12.000 Mb/s +/-0.25 % (2,500 ppm), USB 2.0 section 7.1.11; the bidirectional DShot decoder, host-tested at 4.75 and 5.25 samples a bit (+/-5 %), against an ESC at +/-2 % (V3), leaves 3 %. The CAN controllers take their own 40 MHz clock (IOBoard.md, Controller clock), so the CAN bit rate does not depend on this crystal

found_values.value: Load capacitance 10 pF; ESR at most 50 Ohm; drive-level rating at least 200 uW. RP2350 Table 597 gives the crystal the XOSC is specified with, the ABM8-272-T3: CL 10 pF, ESR (R1) 50 Ohm max, drive level 10 uW typical and 200 uW max. Hardware design with RP2350, section 4: a maximum ESR of 50 Ohm 'along with a 1 kOhm series resistor (R2), is a good value to prevent the crystal being over-driven and being damaged when using an IOVDD level of 3.3 V'; two 15 pF capacitors plus 3 pF parasitic give '10.5pF, which is close enough to the target of 10 pF'. Neither document states the drive level the circuit applies; the 200 uW rating of the specified crystal is taken as the lowest rating a crystal may have

found_values.value: At most 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground on each of D+ and D-, shared by the RP2354B's USB pin, the connector and the protection, with D+ and D- differing by less than 10 %. USB 2.0 section 7.1.6.1: the upstream facing port of a full-speed device with a detachable cable may have 100 pF (CINUB), 'comprised of up to 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground on each line at the transceiver and in the connector and an additional 25 pF capacitance on each conductor in the transmission line'; 'The difference in capacitance between D+ and D- must be less than 10%'. The RP2350 datasheet gives no capacitance for USB_DP and USB_DM (Table 1437), so the share left for the protection is not known

report.value: 13 errata affect stepping A4: E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8, E11, E12, E17, E26, E27, E28. None constrains a pin, a pull resistor or an input front end on A4: E9 (increased Bank 0 leakage with the pad input enabled) affects A2 only, fixed on A3 (PCN 28); E3 (QFN-60 GPIO_NSMASK) and E16 (USB_OTP_VDD and OTP reads) are A2 only. Those that constrain a peripheral: RP2350-E5 (DMA, A2 to A4), interactions between CHAIN_TO and ABORT of active channels; workaround: before aborting an active channel, clear the EN bit of the aborted channel and of any channel it chains to; cited by firmware/iomcu/src/out_ppm.c. RP2350-E8 (DMA, A2 to A4): CHAIN_TO might not fire for zero-length transfers; workaround: do not use CHAIN_TO with zero-length transfers. RP2350-E12 (USB, 'RP2350 A2, RP2350 A3, RP2350 A4 (mitigated on A3)'): USB status signals not reliably registered when clk_sys is equal to or slower than clk_usb; workaround: run clk_sys at least 10 % faster than clk_usb while the peripheral is in use (52.8 MHz with clk_usb at 48 MHz). RP2350-E27 (bus fabric, A2 to A4): bus priority controls apply to the wrong managers on the APB and FASTPERI arbiters. RP2350-E2 (SIO): SPINLOCK writes mirrored at +0x80. RP2350-E1 (interpolator): OVERF bits broken by right-rotate. RP2350-E11 (XIP cache): clean by set/way modifies the tag of dirty lines. Core, debug and security only: E4 (system bus access stalls with core 1 in clock-gated sleep), E6 (PMPCFGx RWX transposed), E7 (U-mode does not ignore mstatus.mie), E17 (guarded OTP read fault), E26 (RCP random-delay side channel), E28 (OTP keys for pages 62/63 applied to all lock words)

report.value: The RP2350 watchdog counts down in microseconds from LOAD (24 bits, up to 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds', Table 1249), is disabled at reset (CTRL.ENABLE 0x0) and pauses in debug (PAUSE_DBG0, PAUSE_DBG1, PAUSE_JTAG reset 1, Table 1248). Against the stop deadline (V1, 500 ms): the part can set any timeout under 500 ms; the time from expiry to the pads at their reset state is not stated. Against the longest legitimate stall (V2 as found): 900 ms for a pass with a 400 ms packaged-part sector erase and one 500 ms blocked console write, and no bound with a host that keeps accepting slowly, since each accepted chunk restarts pico-sdk 2.3.0's 500,000 us PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US, which the tree does not override. So no timeout meets both while the firmware erases flash in the loop and the console write is uncapped. A window opens once the store moves to the FRAM (Q8) and the console write is capped below 500 ms less the rest of the pass and the reset; the cap is not stated. The image sets no timeout (V4). For the owner: the console-write cap and the timeout, in firmware. Not a defect of the part
report.source: RP2350 datasheet build-version d126e9e-clean (SHA-256 2877d0f2...4be8), section 12.9, Tables 1248 and 1249, read 2026-10-02T06:22:39Z; V1; V2 and V4 as found; pico-sdk 2.3.0 stdio_usb.c and stdio_usb.h, read 2026-10-02T06:23:55Z; firmware/iomcu/src/main.c in checkout fe53d3a8bc9a

report.value: pico-sdk 2.3.0 _watchdog_enable() sets every PSM_WDSEL bit except ROSC and XOSC (watchdog.c, the line after '// Reset everything apart from ROSC and XOSC'); WDSEL bit 4 is RESETS (Table 532), and the RESETS register resets with PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) held in reset (Table 535). Section 9.7: 'resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state, but has no effect on isolated pads'; the ISO bits are not reset by that block reset. The SDK clears a pad's ISO bit in gpio_set_function(), so a pad in use returns to its reset state (section 9.3: output high-impedance through the null function, input disabled, pulled low). A pad left isolated keeps its latched state. Section 9.3's list of events that return the pads to their reset state names brownout, RUN low, SW-DP CDBGRSTREQ and RP-AP rescue reset, not the watchdog. The image enables no watchdog yet (V4). Not measured

A fourth single part, DT1240-08LP3810-7 (8 lines to a common clamp, no supply pin, VRWM 5.5 V, +/-14 kV contact, +/-16 kV air, 9 V at 10 A TLP), passes every value and rule 4 (JLCPCB 125) but fails rule 5 (Digi-Key 0); FU-2A dropped it on a superseded datasheet revision that described four I/Os. Parts that steer their data lines to a VBUS pin (VBUS54CV-HSF-G4-08, USBLC6, IP4234, NUP4114) do not carry CC, because a Type-C source drives CC to vRd, 0.277 to 2.042 V, while VBUS is at vSafe0V before attach. Every passive clamp passes V12's 3.63 V steady limit only by the relaxation: none limits a steady voltage below its breakdown, 6 V min or more. Ranking grounds, each breaking a tie on the ones before: (1) rule 5 passes; (2) fewest values resting on the relaxation, on application text or on typical-only figures; (3) maker status read at the maker; (4) JLCPCB stock

found_values.value: Barrier pack-side current, from the always-on pack-side supply's 5 V rail (not from VREG, owner 2026-10-02). Rank 1 ISO7741DWR at VCC2 = 5 V: ICC2 2.8 typ / 4.6 mA max at 1 Mbps and 4.2 / 6.4 mA max at 10 Mbps, all channels switching, CL 15 pF; DC 2.0 / 3.7 mA max with inputs high and 3.2 / 5.2 mA max with inputs low. The 1 MHz SPI clock is 2 Mbps, between the tabulated rates, so 6.4 mA bounds it; the idle monitor (CS and SCK high, SPI mode 3) draws 3.7 to 5.2 mA. Rank 2 ISO6741DWR: 4.5 mA max at 1 Mbps, 6.5 mA max at 10 Mbps, DC 3.5 / 5.1 mA max. Rank 3 ISOW7741BDFMR, IISOIN from its own isolated converter at 5 V: 7.1 mA max at 1 Mbps, 8.9 mA max at 10 Mbps, DC 7.9 mA max. Mixed 3.3 V / 5 V supplies are not tabulated for ISO7741 or ISO6741

Awake: ADBMS1818 VREG 16.5 mA (measure) + 8.1 mA (ISOMD = V-, active, RB1 + RB2 = 2 kOhm; 3.3 mA with 20 kOhm) + ISO7741 6.4 mA = 31.0 mA at most. Asleep: VREG 9 uA + ISO7741 3.7 to 5.2 mA

report.value: TME needs V+ at or above C18 - 0.3 V, and C18 may not exceed V+ + 5.5 V (absolute). With unused inputs tied to the top cell, C18 is the pack top. A fixed 18 V supply alone (17.7 V after a 0.3 V OR drop) misses TME for packs above 18.0 V (5 cells at 4.2 V, 21.0 V) and exceeds the absolute limit above 23.2 V (6 cells at 4.2 V, 25.2 V). V+ must also be fed from the highest connected tap; with no count setting (V193) that tap moves from C1 to C16, so the feed takes an OR element from each tap that can be a pack top, or another circuit. No function names it. A gap for P5 and P6
report.source: ADBMS1818 Rev. B Tables 3 and 11, p. 86; V193; F15

found_values.value: A magnetic angle sensor of its own at the horn, which R11 selects: a sensor board JLCPCB assembles, under a diametric magnet fixed on the horn's axis, read over one of the 2 external Qwiic I2C ports at 3.3 V behind the TCA9548A (Q7). The F4 encoder is not the source: F4 lets the operator mount it on the servo output shaft or the motor shaft, so with it on the motor shaft the servo screen's measured arm has no input, and a servo test then needs the encoder moved. When the encoder sits on the servo output shaft the firmware may read it as well; the decode is the function 'encoder decode'. An accelerometer on the surface is not the source: it cannot observe rotation about the gravity vector
found_values.source: checkout fe53d3a8bc9a: hardware/docs/Research.md:672 (F4, owner 2026-09-25), :913 (V209 choices); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:82 (External sensors, Q7), :493 (Servo measured position); docs/Screens.md:156-158; hardware/docs/Pins.md:115-116, :123 (Qwiic bus and TCA9548A on the measurement coprocessor)

found_values.value: 0.129 degree or finer over 180 degrees of horn travel (+/-90). The servo screen maps the horn's full travel of 180 degrees onto the servo type's pulse span (us_to_deg: deg = (us - centre - trim) x 90 / (span / 2)) and takes the measured position as a whole number of microseconds (servo_screen_feedback(uint16_t position_us, ...)). One microsecond is 180 / 1000 = 0.18 degree on STANDARD (1000 to 2000 us), 180 / 1400 = 0.129 degree on WIDE (800 to 2200 us) and 0.9 degree on NARROW 760 (660 to 860 us); the sensor resolves the finest, 0.129 degree, so the link's 1 us step is the limit

The panel already enables and places a rotation input by setting (SET_OPTICAL_EN, SET_OPTICAL_PIN), and the BENCH page carries one rpm register (LINK_BN_RPM = 3) with one valid bit (LINK_BN_RPM_OK, bit 2). found_values.value: 1.244 us of delay variation at 1,092 Hz (65,535 rpm) for the optical index: the sensor, its front end and the index comparator together. 1 degree of the 915.5 us period at 65,535 rpm is 2.543 us for the whole chain (V225); R10's own share is 52 ns, the ADCS7476's 30 ps aperture jitter and the chip-select trigger's jitter inside, with no SPI contention (V290, V291); V290 gives the accelerometer and the optical index 1.244 us each. At 10,000 rpm the split gives 8.16 us each. Per docs/Balance.md:65-66 a constant delay cancels because the trial run measures the whole chain, so the share bounds the delay's change between the runs of one balance

requirements.name: count rate
requirements.datasheet: not a datasheet figure; derived from the datasheet's timing and not run on hardware. Each state machine fetches, decodes and executes one instruction a system clock cycle (11.2.2); quad_edge.pio (19 words) runs one state machine per channel, at most 6 cycles from an edge to the next WAIT (40 ns at 150 MHz) against 100 ns between one channel's edges at 5 MHz (80 ns at 40/60 duty). The cycle model with the 2-flipflop input synchroniser (11.5.6.3) decodes 40,000 counts at 5 MHz without error
requirements.source: RP2350 datasheet build-date 2025-07-29, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf, vendors.py fetch, read 2026-10-02T00:29:31Z (FU-2C); quad_sim.py and quad_edge.hex (FU-2C, sha256 60d783a6... and 1681c9c6...) re-run in /home/claude/rcbench-research/round2/scratch/FU-2D/P2-R11/ 2026-10-02T06:32:05Z to 06:32:13Z: 40,000 of 40,000 counts at 5 MHz with 50, 40 and 60 % duty and 3 ns jitter, 1388 net counts through 200 reversals, -3022 at 1 MHz through 50 reversals; A-to-B spacing decoded down to 14 ns, failing at 13 ns; longest edge path 6 cycles

requirements.name: direction
requirements.datasheet: on each edge of its channel a state machine samples the other channel with JMP PIN: low counts in X, high in Y, reversed on the other edge; net = Y(A) - X(A) + X(B) - Y(B) modulo 2^32, which matched the true count through 200 reversals at 5 MHz and 50 at 1 MHz

report.value: PIO state machines on the measurement coprocessor: 2 state machines in PIO0, one per channel, each running one copy of the 19-word quad_edge.pio (13 of the block's 32 instruction words left), RX FIFOs joined in put mode (FJOIN_RX_PUT); 0 DMA channels; 0 PWM slices; GPIO 20 (A), 21 (B) and 22 (I, the index, captured by a GPIO edge interrupt on the 1 us system timer or a third state machine; firmware's choice, not written). No external decoder: none from an allowlisted maker is in the jlcparts copy (LS7366R, LS7184, LS7183 and LS7083 are LSI/CSI). The cycle model at clk_sys 150 MHz with the 2-flip-flop input synchroniser decodes 40,000 of 40,000 counts at 5 MHz per channel (20 Mcounts/s) at 40, 50 and 60 % duty with 3 ns jitter, the net count through 200 reversals at 5 MHz and 50 at 1 MHz, and A-to-B spacings down to 14 ns (13 ns fails); AM26LV32EIDR leaves 32 ns. Longest path from an edge to the next WAIT: 6 cycles, 40 ns. Not run on hardware; the program is not in the tree
report.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, sections 11.2.2, 11.3, 11.4, 11.5.6.3 (FU-2C P2 reading 2026-10-02T00:29:31Z); quad_sim.py and quad_edge.hex from FU-2C re-run in /home/claude/rcbench-research/round2/scratch/FU-2D/P2-R11/ at 2026-10-02T06:32:05Z to 06:32:13Z; hardware/docs/Pins.md:117-119, :166-168

report.value: No accelerometer shows the 1.244 us share at 1,092 Hz. ADXL316 and ADXL326 require CX of 4.7 nF or more ('Capacitors must be added', 'A minimum capacitance of 0.0047 uF ... is recommended in all cases'); with RFILT 27 to 37 kOhm (ADXL316) or 32 kOhm +/-15 % (ADXL326) the pole's delay at 1,092 Hz spans 104.40 to 127.26 us, a variation of 22.86 us (ADXL316), and 21.94 us (ADXL326). FU-2C's 1.000 us used CX = 100 pF, below that minimum; there the 1,600 Hz 'no external filter' bandwidth (typical only) governs: 87.3 us of delay at 1,092 Hz for a single pole, 0.042 us per Hz of pole movement, so the share allows 29 Hz (1.8 %), which nothing states. docs/Balance.md:65-66 says a constant delay cancels because the trial run measures the whole chain, so the spread between units would cancel; the drift of RFILT, CX and the internal response within one unit between runs is not stated for any part read. The accelerometer keeps no part. The owner decides whether the share is judged on the unit-to-unit spread (fails by 18 x), on the drift within one unit (not stated), or on a measurement
report.source: ADXL316 data sheet Rev. C, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/adxl316.pdf (vendors.py fetch --client safari, read 2026-10-02T06:21:43Z); ADXL326 data sheet Rev. 0, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ADXL326.pdf (vendors.py fetch --client safari, read 2026-10-02T06:28:10Z); computation in this return (delay atan(2 pi f R C) / (2 pi f), f = 1,092.25 Hz)

report.value: Selected on its own values: TLV9062IDR first, AD8606ARZ-REEL7 second (its rule-5 alternate is TLV9062IDR), TSV912IDT third. A unity-gain follower with GBP 8 to 10 MHz typical delays 1,092 Hz by 16 to 22 ns, under the 0.244 us left after FU-2C's 1.000 us; the bound needs GBP above 652 kHz. At the IO board end the ADCS7476's 26 pF sampling capacitor and 400 ns track time need a series resistor and a reservoir capacitor, stage 2 passives whose RC adds its own delay variation: for example 49.9 Ohm +/-1 % and 2.2 nF C0G +/-5 % give 110 ns +/-6.6 ns. The lead's capacitance is not stated (the cable is stage 2's). FU-2C's refutation of ADXL316WBCSZ on 'lead length' is answered by this buffer; the accelerometer fails 'delay variation' instead (report 'accelerometer sensor fit')
report.source: TLV9062 data sheet SBOS839N, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlv9062.pdf (read 2026-10-02T06:26:09Z); AD8605/AD8606/AD8608 data sheet Rev. O, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD8605_8606_8608.pdf (read 2026-10-02T06:26:08Z); TSV91x data sheet DS4899 Rev 13, https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/tsv911.pdf (read 2026-10-02T06:25:21Z); FU-2C/013-P4-datasheet-R10.json (ADCS7476 26 pF, 400 ns)

The edge a pen line gives is also set by the spot size and the bell's surface speed: 1 mm crossing a 28 mm bell at 65,535 rpm takes about 10 us, so a change in reflected amplitude moves the threshold crossing inside that edge by a fraction of it, which no part figure bounds (a bell diameter of 28 mm and a 1 mm spot are assumptions). R10's share of the same budget is 52 ns at 65,535 rpm and 342 ns at 10,000 rpm (V290), with no SPI contention (V291)

TMAG5273A2QDBVR, P2's rank 1, is itself a 3-axis Hall sensor whose angle is computed from X and Y, so 'no angle output' separates the two parts by where atan2 runs, not by a requirement value. The over-temperature maximum counts only where the part is the optical index's comparator, and P2 itself keeps TLV7011DBVR, TLV7031DBVR and TLV1811DBVR for the clip placement alone with no maximum stated at all. exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: This forks on a design choice for the owner. A probe board that carries an infrared emitter and a PIN photodiode, assembled by JLCPCB, is a reflective infrared sensor on a probe board (V219); P2's own readings give the detector times that meet the 1.244 us share (BPV10NF tr 80 ns, tf 60 ns; BPW34 100 ns) where all 9 integrated sensors fail it. The pair has no part-level 'stated operating range' (V220) because the range is a design output, computed from the emitter's stated radiant intensity and the photodiode's stated sensitivity; the pen line's reflectance and width are not stated, and TCND5000's 2 to 25 mm is likewise stated for a reference target, not the pen line. I did not select an emitter or compute the range, and no discrete pair is listed under missed for that reason. TCND5000's own drop holds: its data sheet (Rev 1.6, read 2026-10-02T06:52:01Z) states rise and fall times of 15 ns for the emitter only.

RP2354B is a fixed input of the Scope table: reported to the owner, not re-selected, as FU-A4's and FU-2A's adjudicators ruled. The other 25 checks pass. The time from watchdog expiry to the pads at their reset state is not stated in the datasheet (not measured).

exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: Fail 'chip select idle high' (Pins.md:151-155): the F suffix defaults low on input power loss, which selects the monitor while the host side is unpowered.
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: Pins.md lines 151-155 cover only the coprocessor in reset: pads come out of reset pulled down (32 to 86 kOhm) and each chip select has an external pull-up of about 10 kOhm. In that state the host's 3.3 V rail is up, the barrier input is high and an F part's output is high; F acts only on input power loss. No line of Pins.md, IOBoard.md or Research.md (checkout fe53d3a, read 2026-10-02) states a host-side-unpowered case. In that case an F part holds CSB, SCK and SDI low. ADBMS1818 Rev. B p. 56 (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ADBMS1818.pdf, safari, HTTP 200, read 2026-10-02T07:06:16Z): in SPI mode activity on CSB or SCK wakes the port, and the differential SCK - CSB must reach VWAKE 200 mV for tDWELL 240 ns (Table 7); static low on both lines is 0 mV and no clock edge. No value read shows harm to the ADBMS1818 or to V190. The other values pass: ISO774x SLLSEP4K and ISO774x-Q1 SLLSEU0G (read 2026-10-02T07:02:55Z and 06:51:10Z); ISO6741 not re-read. data.ruling:
The refutation does not hold, and the RP2354B stays for "Microcontroller". The stock verifier refutes nothing. Its verdict is confirmed, its refutation text is empty and all 12 of its checks pass. The datasheet verifier fails 3 checks: watchdog stall cover (V2), watchdog window (V1 and V2) and image watchdog timeout (V4). I re-read the sources, and none of the 3 is a property of the part.

(1) What the part can do. RP2350 datasheet Table 1249 (LOAD, bits 23:0) allows a timeout up to 0xffffff us, "approximately 16 seconds". Table 1248 gives CTRL.ENABLE (bit 30) a reset value of 0x0, so firmware turns the watchdog on. Any timeout below V1's 500 ms (owner, 2026-09-30) can be set. So can any timeout above the 400 ms packaged-part maximum of one W25Q16JV sector erase. The datasheet does not state the time from expiry to the pads reaching their reset state. That time is not read.

(2) V2 and the window. The 900 ms stall is one erase followed by a console printf in the same main-loop pass (firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1049-1089, re-read). With a slow host, pico-sdk's USB console write has no fixed bound. The erase in the loop and the uncapped console write are both choices in the firmware. Moving the store to the FRAM (Q8) and capping the write would remove them. No microcontroller's watchdog covers a stall that has no bound, so the missing window is a firmware gap, not a limit of this silicon.

(3) V4. `grep -rn -i watchdog firmware/ shared/` in checkout fe53d3a8bc9a finds only comments: main.c:970-973, firmware/panel/main/main.c:697 and shared/link/include/link_dev.h:6 and :87. It finds no watchdog_enable, watchdog_update or watchdog_reboot. So "none set" is the value found for V4. It is a firmware gap that IOBoard.md:251 already records ("The image enables none").

The RP2354B is also a fixed input of the Scope table. A fixed input is checked for stock, lifecycle and a second source. One that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. This ruling matches FU-A4 adjudicator-R1 (007) and FU-2A adjudicator-R1 (010), which ruled the same way on the same 3 checks.

Part-level facts I re-read all pass. JLCPCB C39843328 is the RP2354B (Raspberry Pi, QFN-80-EP(10x10), SC1512(13)-A4), with stockCount 2540 and canPresaleNumber 2407. The PCN (product change notice) listing holds only "RP235x A4 stepping PCN", which ends the steppings other than A4. The 20 held parts cover the need of 10.

The scope is function, because the failed checks concern this function's V1, V2 and V4 values in the firmware. None concerns the lifecycle, an end-of-life notice, the maker allowlist or the LCSC identity. For the owner and firmware: the image sets no watchdog timeout, the cap on the console write is not stated, and the expiry-to-reset time is not measured.

data.ruling: The refutation stands. Under tools/research/README.md:459-462 and round1.js:314, this figure checks one thing: whether the function's requirement list names every requirement that IOBoard.md, the answers and the values found for research set for it, with no value weaker than theirs. The table "Microcontroller, flash and debug" in IOBoard.md marks six rows "required" that the claimed list for Microcontroller leaves out: PIO reach, PWM slices, Board header, Image size limit, Flash write window and Store endurance. The R1 category row of Research.md (line 308) also sets two of these on R1 itself. R1 records the in-package flash's erase, program and endurance figures as not known for the die. R1 also records the lines the IO board's pico-sdk header changes from olimex_rp2350_xl.h. The list therefore does not name every requirement set for the function. The fault is in the list, not in the part, so the scope is function. Nothing here concerns the RP2354B's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity. This ruling does not say whether the part meets the omitted rows. The verifier's datasheet readings (12 PIO state machines, 12 PWM slices, 2 MB) were not re-read here and play no part in the ruling. The entries the list does carry are no weaker than their sources: V1 500 ms, V2 and V4 as found, 0 to 50 C, pin ratings, flash supply, SWDIO bias, BOOT and RESET, USB port, crystal and core regulator, and watchdog enabled.
data.evidence:
IOBoard.md in checkout fe53d3a8bc9a, table "Microcontroller, flash and debug". Each row below has the State "required" and is missing from the claim.
- Line 137, PIO reach: "3 blocks, 12 state machines", a block sees 32 GPIO from a base of 0 or 16.
- Line 138, PWM slices: "12 slices of 2 channels", with the slice mapping for GP0-31 and GP32-47.
- Line 143, Board header: PICO_RP2350A at 0 (48 GPIO), 2 MB of flash, no PSRAM.
- Line 144, Image size limit: "2,088,960 bytes: 2 MB less the store's two 4,096-byte sectors".
- Line 146, Flash write window: sector erase 45 ms typical and 400 ms maximum, page program 0.4 ms typical and 3 ms maximum; packaged-part figures, die figures not known.
- Line 147, Store endurance: 100,000 erase cycles a sector; the die's figure is not known.

Research.md line 308 (R1 row): R1 "records its erase, program and endurance figures as not known for the die", and R1 "records the lines the IO board's header changes from" olimex_rp2350_xl.h.

The claimed list (29 entries) names none of these six rows. requirements.datasheet: 3-axis Hall magnetometer (Triaxis); the X and Y outputs under an on-axis diametric magnet give the angle as atan2(By, Bx), which firmware computes; the part has no angle output and no angle engine, unlike rank 1's CORDIC
requirements.source: MLX90393 Rev 012 (18-Nov-2025), https://media.melexis.com/-/media/files/documents/datasheets/mlx90393-datasheet-melexis.pdf, read 2026-10-02T07:08:28Z, features and Section 13

requirements.name: resolution
requirements.datasheet: 16-bit output (NOUT); XY sensitivity 0.161 to 3.22 uT/LSB (Table 9; Table 17 lists 0.150 to 6.009 uT/LSB at HALLCONF 0xC, 25 degC). At 3.22 uT/LSB a step is 0.129 degree or finer for a field in the XY plane of 1.43 mT or more. XY noise (Figure 2, GAIN_SEL 7, read off the plot, approximate): about 51 mGauss at TCONV 1.27 ms, about 11 mGauss at 7.6 ms, about 6 mGauss at 26 ms, so noise stays under 0.129 degree for 0.49 mT or more at 7.6 ms. The magnet's field at the sensor is not stated for this or any candidate. Saturation onset 50 mT; offset drift under +/-1000 LSB and sensitivity drift +/-3 % over temperature (accuracy is not asked by V210)
requirements.source: MLX90393 Rev 012 (18-Nov-2025), https://media.melexis.com/-/media/files/documents/datasheets/mlx90393-datasheet-melexis.pdf, read 2026-10-02T07:08:28Z, Table 9, Figure 2, Table 17, Table 19
